text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: multiple CUDA OOMs and container restarts observed in us-east-dedicated pool (paged-attn allocator). Auto-alerting / escalations triggered.

maya (oncall): seeing steady rise in OOMs since ~12:05 UTC, node flaps starting to appear. Initial spike aligns with batch jobs from customer: corp-x.

liam (eng-runtime): confirmed. stack traces show paged-attention allocation failures -> fragmentation. KV cache growth is high on affected containers.

arjun (eng-sre): getting node-level metrics: memory_pressure + page-faults increasing. Docker restart loops on 3 of 7 pods in pool-7.

sam (support): flagged 2 Dedicated customers reporting 503s and very high latency. Support ticket IDs: #5281, #5282. Customers notified with ACK, we need ETA.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce kv_cache_max to 20% on pool-7 2) force local KV eviction 3) bounce affected runtime containers 4) route traffic to fallback models/regions. I'll start 1 & 2 now.

liam (eng-runtime): +1. Patch we deployed last week changed paged allocator free-list coalescing; looks like fragmentation is slowly creeping. Workaround: disable paged attention on high mem requests and fallback to non-paged path.

maya (oncall): running command to shrink KV cache for pool-7:

```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/pools/pool-7/config 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN' 
  -d '{"kv_cache_max_bytes": "0.2"}'
```

incident-bot: Action recorded by maya at 12:18 UTC.

ops-bot: Triggering graceful restart for pods: runtime-7a, runtime-7b, runtime-7c. Rolling with 30s stagger.

jen (customer-sre): I'm drafting an update for Corp-X and corp-y: telling them degraded perf and partial availability. ETA for full fix?

liam (eng-runtime): temporary mitigation steps implemented: kv limit reduced, eviction run triggered. I'm tailing runtime logs, seeing lower RSS but still intermittent OOM when attention window spikes.

arjun (eng-sre): added cgroup mem.limit_in_bytes bump on node-3 to avoid immediate oom-kill while we stabilize. Note: this is a risky temporary measure.

maya (oncall): handoff: liam is primary for runtime hotfix, arjun for node-level mitigations. I'll stay on thread for customer comms. Next oncall rotate in 2h -> handoff note will be posted.

liam (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: paged-attn allocator fragmentation + KV cache retention causes slow-growing unfreeable fragments. When attention page size hits threshold, allocator can't satisfy and triggers a fallback that still grows native allocations -> gradual mem creep to OOM.

liam (eng-runtime): quick diagnostic commands I'm running:

```bash
# check free-list fragmentation stats (internal metrics)
curl -s http://runtime-7a:9000/metrics | grep paged_allocator_free_frag
# dump KV cache sizes
redis-cli -h kv-backend SCAN 0 MATCH pool-7:* COUNT 1000 | xargs -L1 redis-cli HGETALL
```

maya (oncall): Support update posted to #support: "We're mitigating a memory fragmentation issue impacting some dedicated nodes. We've applied temporary limits and are routing traffic to alternate capacity; expect partial availability recovery within 30-45m." :hourglass: 

sam (support): customers responded: corp-x asks for IP allowlist to failover to their fallback. corp-y asked for ETA; pushing updates every 15m.

liam (eng-runtime): local hotfix branch created: allocator:coalesce-v2 — reworks free-list coalescing and adds per-kv eviction markers so fragments can be reclaimed faster. Running unit + fsan tests. If green, I'll prepare a canary to dedicated-scan-1.

deploy-bot: Canary build queued: build-2461 -> canary deploy to dedicated-scan-1.

arjun (eng-sre): I'm preparing node snapshot + core dumps for the 3 flapping pods. Also enabling additional verbose GC logs to track frees.

maya (oncall): live mitigation status: kv caps in effect, 3 pods restarted (staggered), traffic shifted ~40% to fallback region, customer impact reduced but some 503s persist. Monitoring.

liam (eng-runtime): if canary passes we can push hotfix to pool-7 with rollout strategy: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with auto-rollback on OOM increase. Also recommend enabling 'evict-on-prefetch' flag to avoid prefetching huge attention pages.

jen (customer-sre): I'll coordinate customer-facing postmortem timeline: preliminary root cause within 24h, permanent patch ETA 48-72h depending on canary.

maya (oncall): handoff note for next oncall (in 2h): state = stabilizing; active mitigations = kv limit, per-node cgroup bump (temp), restarts done, canary pending. Primary contacts = liam, arjun. Pager schedule updated.

incident-bot: Incident severity lowered to P2 at 12:52 UTC as error rates drop but some customers still affected.

sam (support): logging follow-up tickets and marking customers who require pro-rate credits.

liam (eng-runtime): follow-ups: add fragment-size histograms to telemetry, add early-evict path for large KV entries, harden coalescing in allocator. I'll open PR and link here when ready.

maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll continue monitoring and will post final update after canary or if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Thread closed for now but will reopen on new alerts."
